subject: english
title: Word Twins
objective: Identify synonyms and antonyms by comparing word meanings.
introduction: Milo finds word cards that either share a meaning or point in opposite directions. Can you spot the relationship in each pair?

vocabulary.definition: two words that name nearly the same feeling or idea
two words that both describe starting something
two words whose meanings point in opposite directions

activities.instruction: Read each pair and compare what the two words mean.
activities.content: Synonyms have similar meanings; antonyms have opposite meanings.

feedback.retry: Compare the two ideas again: same meaning or opposite meaning?

activities.prompt: Learn how synonyms share meaning and antonyms show opposites.
activities.narration: Synonyms have similar meanings, while antonyms have opposite meanings. Compare the ideas, not just the spelling.
activities.guideHint: Ask: do the words mean nearly the same, or do they point in opposite directions?
activities.accessibilityAlternative: Synonyms have similar meanings, while antonyms have opposite meanings. Compare the ideas, not just the spelling.

activities.instruction: Tap each pair that shows a word relationship.

feedback.retry: Check whether the pair shares a meaning or shows an opposite.

activities.prompt: Find pairs whose meanings match or oppose each other.
activities.narration: Related words may share a meaning, such as happy and glad, or show opposites, such as hot and cold.
activities.guideHint: Read both words and think of what each one means.
activities.accessibilityAlternative: Related words may share a meaning, such as happy and glad, or show opposites, such as hot and cold.

activities.instruction: Sort pairs with a clear relationship from unrelated pairs.

feedback.retry: Say the relationship aloud before placing the pair.

activities.prompt: Sort each pair by whether its meanings match or oppose.
activities.narration: A related pair has a clear same-meaning or opposite-meaning rule. An unrelated pair does not.
activities.guideHint: Test the pair: can you state how the two meanings connect?
activities.accessibilityAlternative: A related pair has a clear same-meaning or opposite-meaning rule. An unrelated pair does not.

activities.instruction: Tap the pair whose words have similar meanings.

feedback.retry: Look for two words that name nearly the same idea.

activities.prompt: Choose the pair that names nearly the same feeling.
activities.narration: Synonyms name nearly the same idea, so happy and glad belong together.
activities.guideHint: Say what each word means and compare the ideas.
activities.accessibilityAlternative: Synonyms name nearly the same idea, so happy and glad belong together.

activities.instruction: Match each pair to the relationship it shows.

feedback.retry: Check whether the two meanings match or point in opposite directions.

activities.prompt: Match each word pair with its meaning relationship.
activities.narration: The relationship may be same meaning or opposite meaning; the rule explains why the pair belongs together.
activities.guideHint: Read the pair, then choose the same-meaning or opposite-meaning clue.
activities.accessibilityAlternative: The relationship may be same meaning or opposite meaning; the rule explains why the pair belongs together.

activities.instruction: Put the word-comparing steps in order.

feedback.retry: Check that you read, compared, named, and explained the relationship.

activities.prompt: Order the steps for comparing two word meanings.
activities.narration: Compare each word’s idea before naming the relationship.
activities.accessibilityAlternative: Compare each word’s idea before naming the relationship.

items.prompt: Before the game, Ana feels happy; her brother says she is glad. Which pair shows similar meanings?
items.explanation: Happy and glad both describe feeling good, so they have similar meanings.

items.prompt: A recipe says to begin mixing, then says to start mixing. Which pair shows the same meaning?
items.explanation: Begin and start both tell you to get an action going, so their meanings match.

items.prompt: A cup of cocoa is hot, while ice is cold. Which pair shows opposite meanings?
items.explanation: Hot and cold point in opposite directions on temperature; that is the clue.

items.prompt: The bell rings early, but the bus arrives late. Which pair are antonyms?
items.explanation: Early means before the expected time and late means after it, so they are opposites.

items.prompt: After winning, Jo feels happy and glad. Which pair are synonyms?
items.explanation: Happy and glad both name a good feeling, so they are synonyms.
